## Natural history notes

A microscopic stalked protist characterized by a nearly spherical, lattice-like shell, or test, with many openings through which fine pseudopodia extend. In Florida, Clathrulina elegans would most likely be encountered in freshwater microhabitats such as ponds, marshes, ditches, wetlands, and biofilm-rich surfaces on submerged plants or debris, where it attaches by a slender stalk. It feeds on bacteria, algae, and other tiny microorganisms captured with its delicate pseudopodia, helping recycle nutrients and move microbial production into the broader freshwater food web.
